outcomes.text: Understand the different types of business entity: sole trader; partnership; limited company (including public limited company (plc))
Understand the advantages and disadvantages of these types of business entity.

Understand sources of finance and methods of funding for these types of business entity including: loans (secured and unsecured); bank overdrafts; payment by instalments; rental/leasing as an alternative to purchase; trade credit; sources of finance for limited companies as in 1.5.4.
Use your understanding of types of business entity to take relevant decisions. Note: Questions on Limited Liability Partnerships will not be set.

subtopics.title: Double entry, books of prime entry and accounting records

outcomes.text: Understand the principles of the double entry system to record business transactions.
Understand the accounting equation.
Understand the role of books of prime entry in the recording of business transactions; sales journal; sales returns journal; purchases journal; purchases returns journal; cash book; general journal.
Understand preparation of ledger accounts.
Understand the purpose of a trial balance.
Understand the advantages and disadvantages of maintaining full accounting records.

Understand the accounting concepts underpinning the preparation of accounts: business entity, historic cost, money measurement, going concern, consistency, prudence, realisation, duality, materiality, objectivity, matching /accruals and substance over form.
Understand the use of computerised accounting systems in recording financial transactions.
Understand the advantages and disadvantages of introducing a computerised accounting system.
Understand the ways in which the security of data can be ensured within a computerised accounting system.
Use your understanding of the accounting system to evaluate relevant information and make informed business decisions. Note: Knowledge of specific applications or software is not required.

subtopics.title: Capital and revenue income and expenditure

outcomes.text: Understand the difference between the treatment of capital and revenue income and capital and revenue expenditure.
Understand the effect on profit/loss and asset value of the incorrect treatment of capital and revenue expenditure.
Understand factors that cause the value of non-current assets to depreciate.
Understand the purpose of accounting for depreciation of non-current assets and the associated application of relevant accounting concepts.
Calculate depreciation using the reducing balance and straight-line methods.
Understand the most appropriate method of calculating depreciation.
Measure the value of non-current assets by the cost model or the revaluation model.
Prepare ledger accounts and journal entries for: non-current assets (acquisition and revaluation); depreciation and disposal (including entries for part exchange)
Calculate profit or loss on disposal of a non-current asset.
Record the effect of a charge for depreciation in the statement of profit or loss and statement of financial position.
Understand the need to reconcile and verify ledger accounts using documentation from internal and external sources.
Understand the benefits and limitations of reconciliation and verification procedures.
Understand errors which affect the trial balance.
Understand errors which do not affect the trial balance: omission; commission; principle; original entry; reversal; compensating.
Prepare ledger accounts and journal entries to correct errors using a suspense account.
Understand the effect on the financial statements of the correction of errors.
Understand the benefits and limitations of a trial balance.
Understand updating of cash books.
Prepare bank reconciliation statements.
Understand the benefits and limitations of preparing a bank reconciliation statement.
Understand entries in control accounts.
Understand sales ledger control accounts and purchases ledger control accounts.
Understand reconciliation statements between control account balances and ledger balances.
Understand the effects on financial statements of the correction of errors.
Understand the benefits and limitations of control accounts.
Use your understanding of reconciliation and verification to evaluate relevant information and make informed business decisions.

Calculate and record the adjustments needed and the effect on financial statements in respect of: accruals and prepayments of income and expenses; irrecoverable debts, irrecoverable debts recovered and allowance for irrecoverable debts; depreciation; inventory valuation; correction of errors.
Prepare a statement of profit or loss and statement of financial position for a sole trader from full or incomplete accounting records. The business may be a trading or a service business.

Prepare a statement of profit or loss, appropriation account and statement of financial position for a partnership from full or incomplete accounting records. The business may be a trading or a service business.
Understand why partners may maintain separate capital accounts and current accounts.
Prepare partners’ capital and current accounts.
Understand the contents of a partnership agreement.
Understand the advantages and disadvantages to partners of maintaining a partnership agreement.
Understand the provisions of the Partnership Act 1890 in respect of partners’ salaries, division of profit or loss, interest on partners’ loans, interest on capital and interest on drawings.

subtopics.title: Limited companies: shares, debentures and reserves

outcomes.text: Understand the features and accounting treatment of ordinary shares, bonus issues, rights issues, debentures, dividends and reserves. Note: Questions will not be set on preference shares.
Understand the advantages and disadvantages to the company and to the shareholders of a company making a bonus issue of shares and a rights issue of shares.
Understand the advantages and disadvantages to the company and to the shareholders of a company issuing shares and issuing debentures.
Understand the distinction between capital reserves (share premium and revaluation reserve) and revenue reserves (retained earnings and general reserve)

subtopics.title: Limited companies: ledger accounts and financial statements

outcomes.text: Prepare ledger accounts to record: an issue of ordinary shares at par or at a premium; a rights issue of shares at par or at a premium; a bonus issue of shares. Note: For the purpose of a bonus issue of shares, the revaluation reserve is not to be used.
Prepare a statement of profit or loss, statement of financial position and statement of changes in equity for a limited company. The business may be a trading or a service business.
Understand sources of finance for specified purposes.
Use your understanding of financial accounts of sole traders, partnerships and limited companies to evaluate relevant information and make informed business decisions.

topics.title: 1.6 Analysis and communication of accounting information

outcomes.text: Understand the differing requirements for information of stakeholders including: owners; managers; employees; investors; lenders; suppliers; customers; government; public and environmental bodies.
Communicate and analyse the information required by these different stakeholders.

Calculate key accounting ratios to measure profitability, liquidity and efficiency: profitability ratios: gross profit margin, mark-up, profit margin, return on capital employed, expenses to revenue ratio (operating expenses to revenue ratio); liquidity ratios: current ratio, acid test ratio; efficiency ratios: non-current asset turnover, trade receivables turnover (days), trade payables turnover (days), inventory turnover (days), rate of inventory turnover (times). Note: Candidates must use the formulae given in the appendix to section 3. These are the only formulae accepted in candidate responses.
Evaluate the profitability, liquidity and efficiency of an organisation by interpreting ratios.
Understand possible measures to improve the profitability, liquidity and efficiency of an organisation.
Understand the limitations of accounting information.
Use your understanding of the calculation and evaluation of ratios to make informed business decisions using relevant information.

Use the profitability ratio formulae: gross profit margin (%) = gross profit / revenue × 100; mark-up (%) = gross profit / cost of sales × 100; profit margin (%) = profit for the year / revenue × 100 (can also be expressed as profit for the year (after interest) / revenue × 100); return on capital employed (%) = profit from operations / capital employed × 100, where capital employed = issued shares + reserves + non-current liabilities; expenses to revenue ratio (%) = expenses / revenue × 100; operating expenses to revenue ratio (%) = operating expenses / revenue × 100.
Use the liquidity ratio formulae: current ratio = current assets / current liabilities; acid test ratio = (current assets – inventory) / current liabilities; each answer presented as a ratio.

Use the efficiency ratio formulae: non-current asset turnover (times) = net revenue / total net book value of non-current assets; trade receivables turnover (days) = trade receivables / credit sales × 365 days; trade payables turnover (days) = trade payables / credit purchases × 365 days; inventory turnover (days) = average inventory / cost of sales × 365 days; rate of inventory turnover (times) = cost of sales / average inventory.
Calculate ratios using year-end balances where appropriate, unless the question specifies the use of average figures, and to the number of decimal places required by the question.
Understand accounting for material and labour costs.
Identify and calculate fixed costs, variable costs, semi-variable costs and stepped costs.
Identify and calculate the elements of direct and indirect costs.
Calculate the value of closing inventory using the first in first out (FIFO) and weighted average cost (AVCO) methods (perpetual and periodic)
Understand the principles of just in time (JIT) management of inventory.
Use your understanding of accounting for materials and labour to evaluate relevant information and make informed business decisions.
Apply traditional costing methods to prepare costing statements using unit, job and batch costing principles in both manufacturing and service businesses as applicable.
Understand the difference between a cost centre and a cost unit.
Allocate and apportion overhead expenditure between production and service departments.
Calculate overhead absorption rates using an appropriate basis.
Understand the causes and the calculation of under absorption and over absorption of overheads.
Prepare costing and profit statements using absorption costing.
Understand the uses and limitations of absorption costing.
Understand the usefulness of absorption cost data as a support for management decision-making.
Understand non-financial factors and their significance.
Calculate the contribution of a product.
Interpret a break-even chart. Note: Candidates will not be asked to prepare a break-even chart.
Calculate the break-even point, contribution to sales ratio, level of output or sales to achieve a target profit, and margin of safety.
Understand the use and limitations of break-even analysis.
Prepare costing and profit statements using marginal costing.
Prepare a statement reconciling the reported profits using marginal costing and absorption costing.
Understand the uses and limitations of marginal costing.
Understand the usefulness of marginal costing data as a support for management decision-making, including make- or-buy, special orders, closure of business unit, limiting factors, target profit.
Understand non-financial factors and their significance.
Understand the advantages and limitations of cost–volume–profit analysis.
Understand the usefulness of cost–volume–profit data as a support for management decision-making.
Apply costing concepts to make business decisions and recommendations using supporting data.
Understand non-financial factors and their significance.
Use your understanding of costing to evaluate relevant information and make informed business decisions.
Understand the need for and purpose of financial statements for specific types of business.
Understand goodwill and the difference between purchased goodwill and inherent goodwill.

Prepare partners’ capital and current accounts to record changes required in respect of goodwill and revaluation of assets on: a change in the partners’ profit-sharing ratio; the introduction of a new partner; the retirement of an existing partner; the dissolution of a partnership.
Prepare the partnership appropriation account, statement of profit or loss and statement of financial position including changes in a partnership occurring part-way through an accounting year.
Prepare a realisation account and a revaluation account.
Understand the distinction between a receipts and payments account and an income and expenditure account.
Define and calculate the accumulated fund.

Prepare, from full or incomplete accounting records: a receipts and payments account; accounts for trading and revenue-generating activities; a subscriptions account; an income and expenditure account; a statement of financial position.
Account for other receipts, including life memberships and donations.
Make adjustments to financial statements (as detailed in 1.5.1)
Evaluate possible sources of finance and methods of fundraising.
Prepare a manufacturing account, to differentiate between direct and indirect expenses and to include factory profit.
Prepare, for a manufacturing business, a statement of profit or loss and a statement of financial position.
Account for manufacturing profit and the elimination of unrealised profit from unsold inventory.
Understand the reasons why a business may account for manufacturing profit.

Prepare for a limited company in line with the relevant international accounting standards and legal requirements: statement of profit or loss; statement of financial position; statement of cash flows; statement of changes in equity; schedule of non-current assets.

Use your understanding of the financial accounts of partnerships, clubs and societies, manufacturing businesses and limited companies to evaluate relevant information and make informed business decisions.

Understand the main provisions of each of the following International Accounting Standards (IAS): IAS 1 Presentation of financial statements; IAS 2 Inventories; IAS 7 Statement of cash flows; IAS 8 Accounting policies, changes in accounting estimates and errors; IAS 10 Events after the reporting period; IAS 16 Property, plant and equipment; IAS 36 Impairment of assets; IAS 37 Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets; IAS 38 Intangible assets. Note: For guidance on the scope of each IAS that candidates are expected to be familiar with, teachers are advised to consult the document Teacher Guidance for 9706 Accounting which accompanies this syllabus.
Understand the need for an ethical framework in accounting.
Understand the fundamental principles of: integrity; objectivity; professional competence and due care; confidentiality; professional behaviour.
Understand how the ethical behaviour of accountants and auditors impacts the business and other stakeholders.
Understand the social implications of decision-making.

subtopics.title: Auditing and stewardship of limited companies

outcomes.text: Understand the role and responsibilities of the auditor.
Understand the differences between an external audit and an internal audit.
Understand the difference between a qualified and unqualified audit report.
Understand stewardship and the role of directors and their responsibilities to shareholders.
Understand the importance of a true and fair view in respect of financial statements.
Use your understanding of ethical considerations and auditing to evaluate relevant information and make informed business decisions.
Understand the nature and purpose of the merger of different types of businesses to form a new business entity.

Prepare journal entries and make entries in the relevant ledger accounts to record the: merger of two or more sole trader businesses to form a partnership or a limited company; merger of a sole trader’s business with an existing partnership to form a new partnership; acquisition of a sole trader’s business or partnership by a limited company.
Calculate the value of goodwill on the acquisition of a business by another entity.

Prepare statements of profit or loss and statements of financial position for the newly formed business entity following the acquisition or merger, for example the limited company acquiring the partnership.
Understand the advantages and disadvantages of the acquisition or merger.
Use your understanding of business acquisition and merger to evaluate relevant information and make informed business decisions.
Understand the process of transferring the business accounts to a computerised accounting system.

Understand ways in which the integrity of the accounting data can be ensured during the transfer to a computerised accounting system. Note: Knowledge of specific applications or software is not required.

topics.title: 3.5 Analysis and communication of accounting information

subtopics.title: Analysis and communication of accounting information

outcomes.text: Calculate the following ratios: working capital cycle (in days); net working assets to revenue (sales); interest cover; gearing ratio; earnings per share; price/earnings ratio; dividend per share; dividend yield; dividend cover. Note: Candidates must use the formula given in the appendix to section 3. These are the only formulae accepted in candidate responses.
Analyse and evaluate the results of the ratios and draw conclusions.
Make appropriate recommendations to stakeholders on the basis of the analysis undertaken.
Understand the interrelationships between ratios.
Use your understanding of the calculation and evaluation of ratios to make informed business decisions using relevant information.

Use the solvency and other ratio formulae (A Level only): working capital cycle (days) = trade receivables turnover (days) + inventory turnover (days) – trade payables turnover (days); net working assets to revenue (sales) (%) = net working assets / revenue (sales) × 100, where net working assets = inventories + trade receivables – trade payables; interest cover (times) = profit from operations / interest payable; gearing (%) = fixed cost capital / total capital × 100, which is non-current liabilities / (issued ordinary share capital + all reserves + non-current liabilities) × 100.

Use the investment ratio (stock exchange ratio) formulae (A Level only): earnings per share = profit for the year / number of issued ordinary shares; price/earnings = market price per share / earnings per share; dividend per share = annual ordinary dividend / number of issued ordinary shares, where annual ordinary dividend = interim dividend paid + final dividend proposed; dividend yield = dividend per share / market price per share; dividend cover = profit for the year available to pay ordinary dividend / annual ordinary dividend.
Understand the application of activity based costing (ABC)
Understand the uses and limitations of ABC.
Understand what is meant by a cost driver.
Use ABC to: identify the appropriate cost driver; apportion and allocate overheads; calculate the total cost and selling price of a unit.
Understand the effect of different methods of overhead absorption on cost and profit.
Apply ABC costing techniques to make business decisions and recommendations using supporting data.
Understand the meaning of a system of standard costing in an organisation.
Understand the advantages and disadvantages of a standard costing system.
Understand how standard costing can be used as an aid to improve the performance of a business.

Calculate the following variances: direct material price and usage; direct labour rate and efficiency; fixed overhead expenditure and volume; fixed overhead capacity and efficiency sub-variances; sales price and volume.
Understand possible causes of favourable or adverse variances and their relationship to each other.
Make business decisions and recommendations using supporting data.
Understand the significance of non-financial factors.
Understand the advantages and disadvantages of a budgetary control system to an organisation.
Understand the advantages and disadvantages of preparing budgets using spreadsheets.
Understand what is meant by a master budget.
Prepare the following budgets: sales; production; purchases; labour; trade receivables; trade payables; cash; budgeted statement of profit or loss; budgeted statement of financial position.
Understand the effect of limiting factors on the preparation of budgets.
Understand the benefits of flexible budgeting over fixed budgeting.
Prepare a flexible budget statement.
Understand possible causes of differences between actual and flexible budgeted data.
Prepare a statement reconciling the flexible budgeted cost of production with the actual cost of production.
Prepare a statement reconciling the flexible budgeted profit with the actual profit.
Make business decisions and recommendations using supporting data.
Understand the behavioural aspects of budgeting, including targets, incentives and motivation.
Understand the significance of non-financial factors.
Understand future net cash inflows and outflows arising from the project.

Apply the following capital investment appraisal techniques: payback; accounting rate of return (ARR = (average profit / average investment) × 100); net present value (NPV); internal rate of return (IRR). Note: Questions on discounted payback will not be set. Note: Questions involving a residual value of an investment at the end of a project will not be set.
Understand the advantages and disadvantages of these capital investment appraisal techniques.
Make investment decisions and recommendations using supporting data.
Understand the significance of non-financial factors.
